title: Where lead, antimony and their mixtures melt
description: Bar chart of melting points in degrees Celsius. Antimony, 631. Lead, 327. Lead with about 13 per cent antimony, the lead–antimony eutectic, 247 (National Bureau of Standards, 1936; Wikipedia gives 252 at 12 per cent). Lead with 12 per cent antimony and 4 per cent tin, the three-metal eutectic, 239 (Berger, after Osamura). The ideal-solution estimate for lead and antimony, from their melting points and heats of melting alone, 245 at 8.8 per cent antimony, is this frame's arithmetic.
heading: MELTING POINT · °C
